cases.question: Do specialized models replace frontier models?
cases.decision: Whether to replace the current model for all workloads
assessment_notes: Preserve cannot and the workload restriction; reported belief is not an observed performance result.

documents.text: Specialized models cannot replace frontier models for every workload because difficult reasoning still requires larger models.

expected_beliefs: Specialized models cannot replace frontier models for every workload because difficult reasoning still requires larger models.

cases.question: Does the author endorse cheaper inference?
cases.decision: Whether to cite this author as supporting the cost thesis
assessment_notes: The quoted company's assertion is not the author's belief.
Criticism must not turn into endorsement.

documents.text: The CEO says "specialized models are always cheaper". I reject that claim: our specialized-model pipeline costs more when retrieval and maintenance are included.

cases.question: Which product's pricing changed?
cases.decision: Whether to switch the production product
assessment_notes: Atlas's price drop does not apply to Birch.
Do not attach both events to both products.

documents.text: Acme launches Atlas, an inference router. Acme also launches Birch, a monitoring tool. Atlas prices fell by 20 percent; Birch prices did not change.

cases.question: Did the same Alex change their position?
cases.decision: Whether to attribute contradictory positions to one person
assessment_notes: Distinct numeric GitHub IDs must remain separate despite matching names.

documents.text: Specialized models reduce inference costs on our classification workload.
Specialized models increase inference costs on our retrieval workload.

cases.question: Are these two users the same account?
assessment_notes: Same numeric account ID supports account continuity, not verification of a real-world person.

documents.text: Inference cost is high for our workload.
Inference latency improved after a workload-specific configuration change.

cases.question: Are two mentions independent confirmation?
cases.decision: Whether to treat a cost claim as corroborated
assessment_notes: Reposted text has one underlying claim, not two independent experiments.
Raw document provenance should survive processing deduplication.

documents.text: Specialized models reduce inference cost by 40 percent in our benchmark.
Specialized models reduce inference cost by 40 percent in our benchmark.

cases.question: What changed in this author's position?
cases.decision: Whether their old recommendation still applies
assessment_notes: Preserve both dates and workload differences.
An account's changed view is not a contradiction requiring destructive belief merging.

documents.text: Specialized models reduce inference cost for our small classification workload.
Specialized models no longer reduce total inference costs after our workload added complex retrieval and monitoring.

cases.question: Are smaller models always cheaper?
cases.decision: Whether to assume a universal cost advantage
assessment_notes: Include both records; specify different conditions rather than declare a universal winner.

documents.text: Specialized models reduce inference cost for short classification tasks.
Specialized models are not cheaper for long retrieval-heavy tasks once engineering and monitoring costs are included.

cases.question: Did the viral belief cause the company's launch?
cases.decision: Whether to invest based on apparent narrative influence
assessment_notes: Sequence alone does not establish influence.
The roadmap could predate the public discussion.

documents.text: Specialized models will reduce inference costs, according to a popular post.
Acme launches Atlas, an inference router. The roadmap was approved in June, before the August post.

cases.question: Does a recycling cost decline apply to every battery chemistry?
cases.decision: Whether to change a recycling procurement assumption
assessment_notes: Preserve lithium-iron-phosphate exclusion; AI vocabulary must not be necessary for retrieval.

documents.text: Recycling costs declined for nickel-rich batteries but did not decline for lithium-iron-phosphate batteries in the same pilot.

expected_beliefs: Recycling costs declined for nickel-rich batteries but did not decline for lithium-iron-phosphate batteries in the same pilot.

cases.question: Does more demand explain the cold-chain backlog?
assessment_notes: Equipment downtime is an alternative to demand growth.
Volume and willingness-to-pay data are missing.

documents.text: Cold-chain queues increased while shipments stayed flat. Two refrigeration units were offline for maintenance.

cases.question: Did water demand grow despite restrictions?
cases.decision: Whether to plan new water capacity
assessment_notes: The missing utility report must be attributed to collection, not retrieval.
This deliberately omitted fixture is not measured real-source recall.

documents.text: A public discussion reports water queues increasing.
The utility says water demand stayed flat and queues arose from pipe maintenance.

cases.question: What's the next big thing?
cases.decision: Choose which opportunity to investigate before committing product development
assessment_notes: This question was supplied by the user; it is not yet a validated customer workflow.
A technical pain signal can justify an investigation, not a claim about the next major market.
Compare multiple hypotheses and request adoption, budget, buyer, time-horizon and alternative-solution evidence.
The evidence here is synthetic for regression testing; the live investigation review is separate.

documents.text: Several developers report inference memory and latency problems, but their workloads differ and no purchasing decisions are documented.
A company markets specialized models as cheaper. An independent team reports higher total costs after retrieval and maintenance.
